newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - 10-yr auction jitters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - 10-yr auction jitters.

text.p: With the economic data calendar posing little in the way of a challenge, the U.S. Treasury market looks to remain fixated on supply on Wednesday as the quarterly refunding continues.
After a successful three-year note auction on Tuesday, the Treasury is slated to sell $12.0 billion of 10-year notes Wednesday afternoon.
"Most people think the long-dated paper will be more difficult to move, therefore, I am not optimistic," said Patrick Dimick, bond market strategist at UBS Securities LLC.
Late Tuesday, the when-issued 10-year note was at 6.22 percent.
While that is a heck of a lot more attractive than the 6.00 percent level seen late last week, analysts still believe the issue is not all that enticing.

"The market would like to get it back above 6.25 percent before it would take it down aggressively," Dimick said, adding that 6.25 percent is not necessarily a magic number. "The only way we can save the long auctions is if the curve steepeners come unwound."

Typically, between the two- and five-year note auctions and the quarterly refundings, investors put on curve steepeners. Should they find the need to buy longer dated paper and sell the short stuff, then the auction could go OK, traders said.
Even so, the market still has to worry about Thursday's $10.0 billion 30-year bond auction, which should keep the post-10-year sale reaction limited.
Traders said that the market would like to get the issue above 6.50 percent, from 6.49 percent late Tuesday.

Meanwhile, just 15 minutes after the auction results are due at 1345 EDT/1745 GMT, the Federal Reserve will release its August Beige Book report for the August 19 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Players said the report should be a non-event for the market, much like recent Beige Books.

"It'll show the same story of moderate growth and tight labor markets," said Joe LaVorgna, financial economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "(So), you wouldn't know if it was written 12 months ago or in the current month unless you looked at the cover page."
Others added that since the market does not anticipate a Fed rate hike at the next FOMC meeting, the Beige Book is largely meaningless and is just a recap of what already is known.

More important, players said, is the jobless claims figures and July chain store sales data on Thursday. Analysts said that the chain store sales numbers could prompt revisions to the government's retail sales report.
In late trading on Tuesday, the outstanding 30-year bond was at 101-23/32, down 6/32, to yield 6.49 percent.
